correctness.rationale: Cited primary arxiv:2601.05670v1 Theorem 2.8 supplies floor((n−1)/2)−1 connectivity and Theorem 2.10 supplies lower integral homology rank b(n) and top Z². The only top facets are consistently oriented Hamiltonian paths, hence the two full all-forward/all-backward proper-subset sphere boundaries give two primitive embedded top integral generators. For n≥5, Hurewicz gives lower S^{k(n)} basis, including n divisible by4 where H_{k−1}=0 upgrades (k−2)-connectivity; combining lower and two top sphere maps is an integral homology equivalence between simply connected CW complexes and thus a homotopy equivalence by Whitehead. n=4 mixed ten-bridge/ten-triangle relations kill π1; n=3 has two S2 joined by four bridges; n=2 two disjoint circles. The cited integral theorems are premises, not independently reproved; finite n≤9 checks cannot establish this all-n claim.
